title: Bringing it home
hook: all the year's learning into one day's shape

segments.voice: Yesterday, art and music debates: two girls singing on Eid, and a flute of the family of David. Your line was views differ, voices rise. The questions of today are done. Now, a practice for today. Day one thousand four hundred one.

A river runs past your front door. That's the picture the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, gives his companions in Sahih al-Bukhari. Suppose, he says, in paraphrase, there were a river at someone's door, and he bathed in it five times a day. Would any dirt be left on him? They say no, none at all. That, he says, is the five prayers: through them Allah wipes away wrongs. Not one great washing a year. A river, at the door, every day. This year has gathered a great deal of learning. Today we stop adding, and start arranging it into the shape of one ordinary day.
screen: `A RIVER AT THE DOOR.` → `FIVE TIMES A DAY.` → `FROM LEARNING TO A DAY'S SHAPE.`

segments.voice: Start where the day starts, with intention. The first report in Sahih al-Bukhari says, in paraphrase, that actions are judged by their intentions, and each person gets what they intended. So a day begins before the alarm is off: what is today for? Then the frame. The Qur'an gives it in a line from the chapter called Hud, in Pickthall's translation: "Establish worship at the two ends of the day and in some watches of the night. Lo! good deeds annul ill deeds." The two ends of the day: dawn and dusk, with prayers in between, so that work, school, errands and meals all happen inside a frame, the way a river runs between its banks. Inside that frame go the small things this path has been collecting: the bismillah before eating, the greeting of peace, a word kept kind, a debt remembered, a coin set aside, a minute of Qur'an. None of them is large. And that is the point of the last piece. Al-Bukhari keeps a saying, reported by 'Aisha, that the deeds most loved by Allah are the ones done regularly, even if they are small. Not the heroic weekend. The steady weekday. So the shape of a whole day, in this tradition, is not a schedule of impressive acts. It's a frame of prayer, an intention at the start, small good deeds in the gaps, and a return to the river, again and again. What comes home from a year of learning, in this picture, is not a pile of facts. It is a day that has a shape, and a return to the river.
screen: `FIRST, THE INTENTION.` · `THE TWO ENDS OF THE DAY.` · `SMALL GOOD THINGS IN THE GAPS.` · `REGULAR, EVEN IF SMALL.` · then, large: `A RIVER AT THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: The practice: plan tomorrow as a whole day. Settle, and breathe. Picture waking up tomorrow. What's the first thing you'd like to intend? Hold it. Now move through the day in your mind: the morning, the middle, the afternoon, sunset, night. At each point, place one small thing, a prayer if you pray, a breath, a kind word, a moment of thanks, a few verses read. Keep each one small enough that you could really do it. Don't add more than you can carry. Then picture lying down at night, the day done, the frame held. The bell holds the time.
Bringing it home. Gathering a year's learning into one day's shape: an intention, the frame of prayer, small good deeds done regularly. Today's word.
Your line: a day, whole. Tonight, write down tomorrow's shape in a few lines, one small thing for each part of the day. Tomorrow, your school. Day one thousand four hundred one.

howItsDone: Muslims shape the day around the daily prayers, from dawn to night, and fill the time between with work, family and small acts of worship such as remembrance of Allah, reading the Qur'an and giving.

original.note: Arabic: a regular daily portion of prayer, recitation or remembrance that a person keeps.

trapdoor: what you thought: bringing it home means remembering a year of facts.
what it means: shaping one ordinary day: an intention at the start, prayer at its two ends and between, small good deeds in the gaps.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari's first hadith on intentions, the river at the door, 11:114's two ends of the day, and 'Aisha's report that the most loved deeds are the regular ones, even if small.
